summary: 72 Rubin GPUs and 36 Vera CPUs on the third-generation MGX rack: 18 fanless compute trays, 9 NVLink 6 switch trays, 4 x 110 kW power shelves, 45 °C inlet water. Early access since September 2026; power, weight and price are estimates.

nominalPowerW.note: NVIDIA has not published rack power. ModulEdge puts VR200 NVL72 at roughly 190 to 230 kW; midpoint used.

peakPowerW.note: Gigabyte's VR NVL72 POD page lists rack power up to 240 kW (seen in search results; the page returned 403 when fetched). Consistent with 4 x 110 kW shelves run redundant (220 kW per side) plus headroom.

weightKg.note: Not published. Started from GB300 NVL72 at 1,580 kg, added the deeper and taller rack (1,200 x 2,300 mm vs 1,068 x 2,236 mm), the liquid-cooled busbar and about twice the coolant flow, and took out the tray fans. About +15%.

widthMm.note: Civo rack spec table: 600 x 1,200 x 2,300 mm.

maxLiquidFraction.note: Compute and switch trays are fully liquid cooled (Civo: 100% direct liquid), but NVIDIA's guide says the power shelves use air-cooled PSUs. About 2 to 3% PSU loss plus the two management switches go to air.

capexUsd.note: Morgan Stanley bill-of-materials estimate of about $7.8M per rack for hyperscalers (via PC Games Hardware). Later analyst figures driven by HBM4 prices run to about $9.1M.

leadTimeWeeks.note: Early access since September 2026, volume ramp in the second half of 2026 (ModulEdge); Cisco says availability dates are to be announced. Assumed 26 to 40 weeks for orders placed now.
